headline: London olive oil prices falling towards £9.03 as harvests recover

cards.title: Satellites and news
cards.text: Spanish olive canopy greenness jumped 14.5% above normal, signaling recovered yields as headlines report falling prices across the European Union.

cards.title: London price impact
cards.text: Olive oil drops from £9.50 to £9.37 in six months, falling to £9.03 at twelve months.

cards.title: Shopping advice
cards.text: Wait to buy olive oil as prices decline, but buy chocolate now before it climbs from £1.85 to £1.91.

vision_notes.text: Vegetation greenness across the olive groves has noticeably increased (+14.5% NDVI vs normal) despite slightly reduced surface water extents. This improved canopy health signals higher olive yields, pointing to increased olive oil supply.

Cloud cover clears to reveal Soubré's canopy, but vegetation greenness is down nearly 9% versus normal. Reduced crop vigor signals lower cocoa yields, pointing to tighter supply and upward pressure on chocolate prices.

Dense, unbroken cloud cover completely obscures the cocoa farms in both images. Ground-level vegetation and canopy health cannot be visually confirmed, leaving cocoa supply conditions unobservable from these scenes.

Vegetation greenness across citrus groves has surged significantly, backed by a 16.9% NDVI rise above normal. This healthier canopy indicates robust crop recovery and increased orange yields, boosting orange juice supply.

Vegetation greenness slightly increased across surrounding fields with stable urban cover and clear skies. This healthy crop vigor indicates steady wheat yields, supporting stable local bread supply and pricing.
